videos.title: The REAL Driving FORCE Behind WORLD Level SIDEPRESSURE & How To TRAIN IT
videos.summary:
World-level side pressure isn’t just about having a stronger arm — and it definitely isn’t about who can tolerate the most pain in their elbow.

That was one of the biggest things I had to understand as I moved beyond national-level armwrestling and started trying to close the gap on genuinely world-class athletes.

We often talk about side pressure as though it’s an isolated arm movement: strengthen the internal rotation, condition the elbow, get comfortable applying force sideways and gradually become capable of handling bigger and bigger loads.

But at the highest level, the arm is only part of the equation.

The REAL driving force behind elite side pressure comes from your ability to connect the hand and arm to the rest of your body — particularly your core — and then transfer that force through the specific lane you’re trying to attack.

And that connection changes depending on whether you’re TOPROLLING, HOOKING or PRESSING.

In this video I break down how I think about engaging the core in each of those positions, how your body should contribute to the movement, and why developing this connection can completely change the amount of pressure you’re capable of producing at the table.

We’ll look at:

• Toproll side pressure — connecting rotation and lateral movement without sacrificing your hand
• Hook side pressure — using the core to drive through an inside position rather than relying purely on the arm
• Pressing — creating a connected structure that allows your body to become the engine behind the movement
• Why simply hammering dynamic side-pressure exercises can eventually become a dead end
• Why elbow pain tolerance is NOT the same thing as world-level side pressure
• How I train the movement to develop force that actually transfers to the armwrestling table

There’s a point where simply making the arm stronger isn’t enough.

Your hand, wrist, arm, shoulder, torso and core have to start functioning as ONE CONNECTED SYSTEM.

When that happens, side pressure stops feeling like your arm is trying to drag your body sideways…

and starts feeling like your entire body is driving through your arm.

That distinction, in my opinion, is one of the major pieces separating strong armwrestlers from genuinely WORLD-LEVEL ones.

If you’ve been training side pressure for years but still feel like everything is happening through your elbow and upper arm, this video may completely change the way you approach it.

Let me know in the comments: when you apply maximum side pressure, where do YOU feel the force coming from?

videos.title: The CHANGE You NEED to Make to go from a NATIONAL Level to a WORLD Level ARMWRESTLER
videos.summary:
There’s a BIG difference between being a successful national-level armwrestler and being genuinely competitive with the world elite.

I learned that difference the hard way.

I became a multiple-time National Champion believing I understood what made an armwrestler strong. Then I started stepping beyond the national level, chasing the best pullers in the world — and some of the assumptions that had taken me that far started falling apart.

One of the biggest?

We massively overvalue back pressure and pronation.

They’re important. They’re measurable. They’re easy to obsess over in training. And because so many elite pullers have incredible numbers in these movements, it’s easy to assume that getting stronger at them is the pathway to becoming world class.

But correlation isn’t necessarily causation.

In this video, I break down what I experienced as I went from being a multiple National Champion to trying to close the gap on world-elite armwrestlers — and the crucial change in thinking that came from it.

I’ll explain where I believe the REAL separation between national-level and world-level armwrestlers starts to appear, why chasing bigger back-pressure and pronation numbers can send your training in the wrong direction, and what I believe you should be prioritising instead if your ambition is to reach the highest level.

This isn’t theory from the sidelines. It’s a lesson built from years of competing, training, winning, losing, experimenting and personally discovering just how different WORLD LEVEL really is.

If you’re already strong, already successful, and wondering why you still can’t bridge that final gap…

This might be the change you NEED to make.

Let me know in the comments: What do YOU think is the biggest physical difference between a national-level and world-elite armwrestler?

videos.title: My Absolute SIDE PRESSURE went from 75kg to 100kg with this ONE LESSON
videos.summary:
My absolute side pressure went from 75kg to 100kg — and the biggest breakthrough wasn’t a new exercise, program, or secret technique. It was finally understanding ONE lesson Todd Hutchings tried to teach me years ago.

Todd told me:

“Pain doesn’t equal weakness. Weakness equals weakness.”

I heard the words back then. But I didn’t truly understand them.

For years, pain during side pressure influenced the way I trained. If something hurt, my instinct was that something must be wrong — that the pain itself was evidence that the structure was weak and that I needed to back away from it.

But what if pain and weakness aren’t the same thing?

In this video, I explain the lesson that finally clicked for me, how it completely changed the way I approached side-pressure training, and how my absolute side pressure progressed from roughly 75kg to 100kg.

This isn't about blindly pushing through injuries or pretending pain doesn't matter. It's about understanding the distinction Todd was trying to teach me — and why that distinction changed the way I think about strength.

After 14 years in armwrestling, sometimes the biggest breakthroughs aren't new information.

Sometimes they're lessons you've already been given… that you're finally ready to understand.

Huge respect to Todd Hutchings for planting this seed years ago. It just took me a while to truly get it.
